subject: social-studies
title: Landscape Change: The Singapore River Mouth, Stage by Stage

questions.prompt: A student says: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the old and new pictures look completely different, so the change must have happened all at once

The change was gradual: the fishing village first became a trading port with godowns and a jetty as trade grew, the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships, and only later did the modern city rise - stage by stage at the same site, with more people living there at every stage.
The village was moved to another island and the city was built in one year on empty land
Nothing changed at the river mouth - the modern buildings were always there behind the huts

questions.misconception: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step. In fact The change was gradual: the fishing village first became a trading port with godowns and a jetty as trade grew, the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships, and only later did the modern city rise - stage by stage at the same site, with more people living there at every stage.

questions.prompt: What were godowns built for at the trading port?

choices.text: For fishermen to mend their nets indoors
To store goods brought by trading ships - waiting to be loaded, unloaded and traded
As houses for the ship captains only
To block ships from reaching the shore

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: as more ships came to trade, godowns were built to store the goods they carried.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what happened at the river mouth as trade grew.
questions.answer: As trade grew, the fishing village became a trading port: godowns were built to store goods, a jetty reached into the water, and more people arrived to work there.
questions.explanation: Scene 2 runs this stage: trade first, then the godowns and jetty, then more people and a climbing people bar.

questions.prompt: Explain why the people bar climbs at every stage of the animation.
questions.answer: Each stage brought more work - first the busy port, then the expanded port - so more people came to live at the river mouth, and the bar climbs stage by stage.
questions.explanation: The people bar rises in s2 and again in s3 and s4: more trade and a bigger port mean more jobs, and more jobs bring more people.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of change at the river mouth in order?

choices.text: Fishing village, trading port with godowns and a jetty, expanded port with warehouses and steamships, modern city
Modern city, expanded port, trading port, fishing village
Fishing village, modern city, trading port, expanded port
Trading port, fishing village, modern city, expanded port

questions.explanation: The whole animation runs the change in that order: s1 fishing village, s2 trading port, s3 expanded port, s4 modern city.
